name: Pedestrian Wind Analysis
tagline: Estimation-grade pedestrian wind-comfort analysis for a real city context, built straight from OpenStreetMap.
description: Builds a 3D city context directly from OpenStreetMap around a pinned location, runs a wind-comfort analysis (colour heatmap plus mean/P95/P99/max statistics per direction), exports the run as HTML/XLSX/CSV/JSON, and generates a PDF report that names the ML surrogate model used and its accuracy limits.

page.objective: Give an early, explainable read on pedestrian wind comfort without commissioning a full CFD study.
page.problem: Pedestrian-level wind comfort is normally assessed by full CFD, which is too slow to run at concept stage.
page.solution: Real building context is pulled from OpenStreetMap around a pinned site, an ML surrogate estimates wind comfort, and the report states the model's own accuracy limits rather than presenting the numbers as exact.

highlights.headline: An OSM-built city context, a wind-speed heatmap, and a report that states its own limits.
points: Build city context from OSM — pins a real-world location and auto-builds the surrounding buildings from OpenStreetMap.
Wind-speed heatmap + stats — a colour heatmap disc with mean/P95/P99/max statistics per wind direction.
Export the analysis run — HTML/XLSX/CSV/JSON, written locally with nothing uploaded.
Auto report, honest limits — a PDF report with an explicit methodology section naming the ML surrogate and its accuracy caveats.
